concept.reason: Actual holotype and hand photograph/Xray suffice.

scope: Original fossil-study target: complete visible skeletal arrangement of genuine plateA PMO214.214, including long limbs, grasping digits and very long segmented tail. Not living furred animal or skull-only substitute.

scale.note: Juvenile specimen dimensions; not adult living size. Curved skeletal length, not straight rectangular bounding box.

diagnostic_targets: Three-dimensional articulated skeletal elements with subtle relief/thickness; never photograph pasted on rectangle.
Short-faced skull with large orbit, rib region, pelvic area and recognizable paired limb bones in plateA arrangement.
Very long tapering segmented tail extending beyond hindlimbs; no coiled prehensile pose.
Separated long manual digits with shorter thumb, large divergent hallux; nail-bearing tips not sharp mammalian claws.
Keep geological support subordinate so skeleton and long tail dominate silhouette.
Use only left image plateA in Figure1; right plateB has fabricated portions and cannot fill gaps.
uncertainties: Crushing, overlapping ribs/limbs and mineral coatings obscure elements. Do not invent missing bones as observed.
Bone depth, backside and thin support geometry are display reconstruction, not CT-complete anatomy.
31preserved caudals reported; last fragment at fault leaves possible1–2more unknown. Do not claim complete originaltailtip.
Avoid definitive human-ancestor claims; use Eocene adapiform primate.
acceptance: Original fossil skeletal scope retained; long limbs and segmented tail structurally recognizable.
Real mesh bone volume visible in oblique and side views, not zero-thickness tracing.
No fabricated plateB completion or unsupported living coat.
ExactGLB fourviews, two reproducible builds, independent QA.

preservation_boundaries.left_lower_leg: Short near-knee fragment only; no distal shaft reconstruction and no left foot
preservation_boundaries.caudal_transverse_processes: Ca1-Ca3 strong; Ca4 reduced at caudal end; none from Ca5 onward
